newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to tap foreign markets for $2.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to tap foreign markets for $2.8 billion.

text.p: Colombia plans to tap foreign capital markets for $2.8 billion in financing next year, including about $1.8 that it hopes to raise through sovereign debt issues, a government official said.
Clemente del Valle, the finance ministry's chief of Public Credit, said the government would request the central bank's authorization for the $1.8 billion in bond issues at the end of this month.
An additional $1 billion in financing will be raised through foreign credits, Del Valle told Reuters in a telephone interview.

The central bank, or Banco de la Republica, initially authorized the government to issue $1.1 billion in sovereign debt in 1996. But the ceiling was raised to $1.4 billion after talks between the bank's board of directors and finance ministry officials in late July.

The government, whose foreign debt is expected to total about $16.2 billion by year-end, reached the limit in new issuance last week with the successful placement of a 275 million mark, five- year floating rate note.
